summary: The reviewed research does not establish a qualifying benefit for this product's assessed use. Existing human research is kept: specific curcumin preparations (for example BCM-95, C3 complex with piperine) show knee-OA and biomarker findings, which belong to formulation-specific records. Dr. Pham's A130 decision rejects broad and generic curcumin benefit language and keeps only a formulation- and indication-specific hold, while this record claims generic Healthy Aging/Longevity. The verified knee-OA biomarker meta-analysis (21 RCTs) pools multi-ingredient products and NSAID add-on arms and reports only surrogate CRP/TNF-alpha changes; the three umbrella syntheses are generic or OA-specific and abstract-only. No credit is possible for this generic claim, so the record becomes reference-only, which removes generic-curcumin Evidence points from dependent products (about 19 per the closure plan). Formulation-specific records (e.g., branded curcumin) are unaffected.

identity.preparation: Different curcumin preparations and delivery systems in disease-specific trials.

population.description: 21 RCTs (2004-2025), 1,705 patients with knee osteoarthritis in seven countries; sample sizes 24-160.

study_contexts.study_design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs of curcumin for knee OA (search to March 28, 2025) pooling pre-post changes in serum inflammatory biomarkers as SMDs.

outcomes.name: CRP SMD -0.906 (95% CI -1.543 to -0.269), P=0.005; TNF-alpha SMD -0.921 (-1.817 to -0.026), P=0.044; ESR, IL-1beta, IL-6 and PGE2 not significantly different.

limitations: Serum biomarkers do not establish cartilage restoration, cancer prevention or universal anti-inflammatory benefit.
TNF-alpha sensitivity and formulation heterogeneity limit inference; preserve enhanced-formulation safety concerns.
Returned decision: Reject broad superiority and generic benefit language; retain formulation/indication-specific hold.
Some included-study citations lack PubMed identifiers in the source XML; retain their exact citations rather than inventing identifiers.

They are publication pointers, not independent-cohort counts, per-primary-study scoring approvals, preparation equivalence or new efficacy evidence. Exact unindexed source citations remain retained; no missing PMID is invented.

3 included source citations have no printed PubMed identifier in this primary source; their exact citations are retained in the source-table receipt. This is a documented identifier limitation, not a fabricated identifier or an extra independent trial.

No credit: knee-OA surrogate biomarkers with multi-ingredient products and NSAID add-on arms in the pool; signed A130 rejects generic benefit language and keeps a formulation/indication-specific hold, and this record claims generic Healthy Aging/Longevity.

dose.reported_regimen: Table 1 formulations range from curcumin 80 mg capsules and BCM-95 500 mg up to 1,500 mg/day curcuminoids with piperine, and include multi-ingredient products (RA-11, Instaflex, CartiJoint Forte, Acujoint with Boswellia, curcumin-gingerol-piperine) and add-on use with diclofenac; comparators include placebo, diclofenac, ibuprofen and glucosamine-chondroitin.

normalization.basis: A heterogeneous synthesis has no single assigned-arm dose. Descriptive regimens do not create an intake recommendation, equivalent preparation or efficacy threshold.
